newsitem.title: India: Bombay shares end mixed in lacklustre trade.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares end mixed in lacklustre trade.

text.p: ** (1030 GMT) - Bombay blue-chips finish mixed
** Foreign funds select buyers in limited stocks
** Benchmark Bombay share index ends 13.30 points higher at
3,263.96 provisional, the days' lowest mark
** National exchange index down 0.13 pts to 936.87,
provisional close
** Trading range-bound, absence of clear market trend,
dealers say
Bombay blue-chips closed a shade higher in a day of little action on Monday, as some late selling tapered off an early rally, dealers said.
The 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) closed 13.30 points or 0.41 percent higher at a provisional 3,263.96, the lowest mark of the session.
"The market is in range-bound trade. There has been demand for blue-chips, but foreign institutions are not aggressive buyers," said dealer Sanjeev Choithani at Pashupati Advani.
The National Stock Exchange index was down 0.13 points at a provisional 936.87.
Traders said buying by foreign funds, active last week, was limited to few stocks. The market was distinctly sluggish on Monday, they added.
"People are generally cautious. Confidence is not building up in a big way," said Sanjay Agarwal, chief executive at Lloyds Finance. "The market is in a wait-and-watch position."
Market participants said one million shares of state-run petroleum firm, Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (BPCL) changed hands in off-market deals at the National Stock Exchange.
The deal was struck between a leading domestic institution and a U S based fund which bought the shares at about 287 rupees, market sources said.
Such deals are not reported in trading volumes at exchanges. BPCL shares closed 1.55 rupees higher at 280.55 on the NSE.
Gujarat Ambuja Cement fell 13.40 rupees to 263.60 after hitting a high of 284.0 in volumes of 195,200 at the NSE.
Exchange officials said they clamped a price limit on the stock after it dropped more than 5 percent on Monday.

At the BSE, SBI rose 1.50 rupees to 231.50, TISCO 1.75 to 191.50, Reliance 1.25 to 212.0 and TELCO 8.25 to 433.25. Hind Lever lost 3.0 to 811.0, Gujarat Ambuja 15.20 to 261.75 and Ranbaxy Lab 4.50 to 629.50 and IPCL 0.50 to 116.75
-- ANSHUMAN DAGA, Bombay newsroom +91-22 265 9000
